title: Post Office Prepares for Holiday Rush & Seeks Emoji Recognition
text:
austrian Post Prepares for Holiday Package Surge, ⁢Seeks ‍Emoji Recognition ⁢for Workers Vienna, Austria – October​ 9, 2025 – AustriaS postal service is already gearing up for its busiest season, announcing plans to bolster staffing and expand ‍its 24/7 service points ahead ⁢of the anticipated Christmas package rush.In a ⁣unique move,⁣ the Post AG also revealed it​ has applied to⁢ the Unicode Consortium for a dedicated ⁤ emoji representing postal workers .
The postal service anticipates a notable‍ increase in volume, with December days possibly seeing twice the package load of a typical summer day, according to postal spokesman Michael Homola. “if you take​ a weak day in July and August, you will have up to twice as much in a single day in December,” he stated.To ⁤manage the surge, the Vienna Post Office, currently staffed by around 1,500 employees, will be hiring additional freight forwarders and temporary personnel. the peak season extends beyond ‍the holidays,⁢ running from‌ mid-November ⁢through‍ January to accommodate returns and voucher redemptions.
Vienna boasts a dense network of over 100 postal branches​ and​ partners,including approximately 280 round-the-clock stations. The Post AG plans to add​ even more ​of these ⁢convenient locations this year.
Coinciding with World Post Day, the request⁢ for a postal worker emoji aims to recognize the vital role of millions ⁢of postal employees globally.Currently, there are around 3,800 emojis, but none specifically representing the profession. ⁣”Emojis⁢ are an integral part of modern communication‍ and ​are ⁢also vital⁤ because they make the daily work of millions of ‍people visible,” Homola explained. “It would be a sign of recognition, inclusion and digital representation for a professional group that connects the world every day.” The idea originated⁣ with an employee in the Post’s press office and has⁢ been met with strong support.
